Melee.name: Small Primitive Weapon
Melee.description:
Small weapons are small one-handed implements no larger than a baton or knife. They are easily concealed in normal clothing, and can even be kept Readied up sleeves or in tailored pockets. Many can be thrown at a range up to 10 meters.

A primitive weapon is one of ordinary metal or wood, with no high-tech augmentations. Primitive weapons are often unable to harm targets in powered armor.

Melee.name: Medium Primitive Weapon
Melee.description: Medium weapons are one-handed swords, axes, spears, or other obvious implements of war. While they can't be effectively concealed in anything smaller than an enveloping cloak or coat, they're also more damaging to an unfortunate victim struck by them. Spears and similar aerodynamic weapons can be thrown up to 30 meters.

Melee.name: Large Primitive Weapon
Melee.description: Large weapons are two-handed implements of bodily ruin such as claymores, halberds, tetsubos, or other such weapons. Unlike smaller weapons, they rely largely on Strength for their employ, and can bash through lighter forms of armor. Large weapons count as two encumbrance items.

Melee.name: Small Advanced Weapon
Melee.description: An advanced weapon has been given a monoblade edge, kinetic sheathing, thermal wires, a chainsaw blade, or some other TL4 touch. Advanced weapons can ignore primitive plate and hide protections.

Melee.name: Medium Advanced Weapon
Melee.description: An advanced medium weapon has been given a monoblade edge, kinetic sheathing, thermal wires, a chainsaw blade, or some other TL4 touch. Advanced weapons can ignore primitive plate and hide protections.

Melee.name: Large Advanced Weapon
Melee.description: An advanced large weapon has been given a monoblade edge, kinetic sheathing, thermal wires, a chainsaw blade, or some other TL4 touch. Advanced weapons can ignore primitive plate and hide protections.

Melee.name: Stun Baton
Melee.description: Stun batons are common law enforcement tools. The damage they do can drop a target to zero hit points, but will not kill them, the victim awakening in ten minutes with one hit point. Stun batons trickle-charge from normal movement and will not run out of electrical energy under normal use conditions.

Melee.name: Suit Ripper
Melee.description: Suit rippers are rods with fractal cutting surfaces designed to cripple vacc suit auto-repair routines. Every hit with a suit ripper counts as a suit tear on a vacc suit-wearing enemy. Unsurprisingly, these weapons are strictly illegal in space environments.

Melee.name: Unarmed Attack
Melee.description: Unarmed attacks reflect ordinary kicks and punches. Unarmed attacks always add the attacker's Punch skill to damage rolls, unlike other weapons.

Ranged.name: Primitive Bow
Ranged.description: Bows are uncommon weapons in the far future, though some lostworlder barbarians have nothing better. Bows can be reloaded with a Move action, or faster if the Gunslinger focus is applied.

Ranged.name: Advanced Bow
Ranged.description: A refined, high-tolerance bow built to modern engineering standards, offering greater range than a primitive bow.

Ranged.name: Conversion Bow
Ranged.description: Some sophisticated conversion bows use special materials to convert the kinetic energy of the draw into a force field "glazing" around the arrow, improving penetration.

Ranged.name: Grenade
Ranged.description: Grenade users always roll to attack AC 10. On a miss, the grenade lands 1d10 meters away from the target in a random direction. Hit or miss, the grenade then explodes for 2d6 damage to all targets within 5 meters. Victims are allowed an Evasion save for half damage. Targets take 1 less point of damage for each point of AC above 14. Grenades can be thrown with the Exert skill instead of Shoot, if desired.

Ranged.name: Crude Pistol
Ranged.description: Crude pistols represent the rawest and most primitive forms of gunpowder weaponry, usually makeshift weapons improvised by criminals or the desperate. Reloading a crude pistol requires two rounds instead of one.

Ranged.name: Musket
Ranged.description: Muskets represent the rawest and most primitive forms of gunpowder weaponry. Reloading a musket requires two rounds instead of one.

Ranged.name: Revolver
Ranged.description: Revolvers are quite popular on frontier worlds, as the weapons are extremely reliable and can be repaired and manufactured even by primitive metallurgists.

Ranged.name: Rifle
Ranged.description: Rifles are the mainstays of most TL2 armies and hunters, thanks to their superior range and power.

Ranged.name: Shotgun
Ranged.description: Shotguns are cheaper and more easily manufactured than rifles, and are popular weapons for home defense on the frontier. Slug rounds do 2d6 damage and have ranges of 50/75 meters.

Ranged.name: Semi-Auto Pistol
Ranged.description: Semi-automatic pistols trade some of the reliability of the revolver for a larger magazine size. They tend to be the favorite sidearm for locals on planets that lack the harsh conditions or uncertain maintenance opportunities of a frontier world.

Ranged.name: Submachine Gun
Ranged.description: Submachine guns take pistol ammunition but fire it at a high rate of speed. These weapons can fire in burst mode.

Ranged.name: Combat Rifle
Ranged.description: Combat rifles are favored by the militaries of tech level 3 worlds, trading some of the often-unnecessary range and penetration of a conventional rifle for a larger ammunition capacity and burst fire capabilities. On more strait-laced worlds such military weaponry is often illegal for civilians to possess.

Ranged.name: Combat Shotgun
Ranged.description: Combat shotguns are more complicated and temperamental versions of conventional shotguns. These weapons have substantially larger ammunition capacity and are capable of firing in burst mode.

Ranged.name: Sniper Rifle
Ranged.description: Sniper rifles are designed to be exceptionally effective at dropping unsuspecting targets at long range. Any target it mortally wounds via an execution attack will die instantly, with no chance for stabilization.

Ranged.name: Void Carbine
Ranged.description: Void carbines are designed for vacuum and zero-gee use, and have essentially no recoil. Their rounds cannot penetrate ordinary ship equipment plating.

Ranged.name: Mag Pistol
Ranged.description: Mag weaponry involves the magnetic acceleration of metal flechettes. Mag ammunition is packaged with integral power supplies, so no additional power cells are necessary to fire these weapons.

Ranged.name: Mag Rifle
Ranged.description: Mag weaponry involves the magnetic acceleration of metal flechettes. Mag ammunition is packaged with integral power supplies, so no additional power cells are necessary to fire these weapons.

Ranged.name: Spike Thrower
Ranged.description: Spike throwers are the shotgun equivalents of mag weaponry, magnetically accelerating a spread of flechettes. Mag ammunition is packaged with integral power supplies, so no additional power cells are necessary to fire these weapons.

Ranged.name: Laser Pistol
Ranged.description: Laser pistols and laser rifles are the most common type of energy weapon. The lack of recoil for non-Heavy energy weapons makes them more accurate, granting a +1 bonus to hit rolls. One Type A power cell is sufficient to recharge an energy weapon's magazine.

Ranged.name: Laser Rifle
Ranged.description: Laser pistols and laser rifles are the most common type of energy weapon. The lack of recoil for non-Heavy energy weapons makes them more accurate, granting a +1 bonus to hit rolls. One Type A power cell is sufficient to recharge an energy weapon's magazine.

Ranged.name: Thermal Pistol
Ranged.description: Thermal pistols and their larger, two-handed plasma projector cousins replace the beam of a laser with a small sphere of magnetically-shaped plasma. The spheres tend to dissipate at much shorter ranges than a laser beam, but do significantly more damage to targets within range.

Ranged.name: Plasma Projector
Ranged.description: Thermal pistols and their larger, two-handed plasma projector cousins replace the beam of a laser with a small sphere of magnetically-shaped plasma. The spheres tend to dissipate at much shorter ranges than a laser beam, but do significantly more damage to targets within range and are not affected by ambient particulates.

Ranged.name: Shear Rifle
Ranged.description: Shear rifles are the product of a relatively few functioning pretech manufactories. These weapons use miniaturized grav projectors to create dangerous repulsor fields inside a target, tearing the object apart along perfectly smooth planes. Shear rifles are completely silent in operation.

Ranged.name: Thunder Gun
Ranged.description: Thunder guns are named for the basso vibrations caused by their operation, a sound that can be felt as far as thirty meters away from an operator. This two-handed weapon uses grav plates to create rapid, randomized disruptions in a target. If a thunder gun hits a target with an unmodified hit roll of 16 or higher an extra 1d10 damage is rolled; this bonus damage always applies to inanimate targets.

Ranged.name: Distortion Cannon
Ranged.description: Distortion cannons are among the most sophisticated man-portable weapons designed before the Scream, manipulating the underlying fabric of space to disrupt a target. Provided the wielder can see a target within range or accurately fix its location within one meter, the distortion cannon can ignore up to one meter of solid cover between the gun and its target.

Heavy.name: Rocket Launcher
Heavy.description: Rocket launchers cover a wide variety of man-portable missile launchers of varying degrees of sophistication. The weapons are usually equipped with basic tracking sensors, but are of limited accuracy against human-sized targets, taking a -4 hit penalty against them. Unlike most Heavy weapons, rocket launchers can be shoulder-fired without a prepared emplacement to support them.

Heavy.name: Demo Charge
Heavy.description: Demo charges are the general run of placed explosives beloved of terrorists and adventurers the world over. The usual variety can be detonated by radio signals, timers, or electrical charges, and inflict their damage on any objects within twenty meters, with an Evasion saving throw for half damage. Victims within forty meters take half damage, with an Evasion save for none. PCs with a background in demolitions or Fix-0 skill can shape the charge so it directs the blast in only one direction, sparing all but two meters of the rest.

Primitive Armor.name: Shield (Primitive)
Primitive Armor.description: Primitive shields are usually of wood or stretched hide. If the bearer is already wearing equal or better armor, the shield simply grants a +1 bonus to their AC. Shields also render the bearer immune to the first instance of melee Shock they might otherwise suffer in a round. All shields require one free hand to use effectively.

Primitive Armor.name: Leather Jack
Primitive Armor.description: Leather jacks, thick hides, and quilted armor are catch-all coverings for armor technology that lacks access to advanced materials and processes. While such armor can be very effective in protecting against primitive weaponry, it is useless against advanced TL4 melee weapons and firearms of all kinds; against these weapons, it is treated as AC 10.

Primitive Armor.name: Cuirass
Primitive Armor.description: Cuirasses, brigandine, linothorax, and half-plate are sturdier primitive armor varieties, offering good protection but useless against advanced TL4 melee weapons and firearms of all kinds.

Primitive Armor.name: Full Plate
Primitive Armor.description: Full plate and layered mail represent the best protection a primitive world can produce, though it remains useless against advanced TL4 melee weapons and firearms of all kinds.

Street Armor.name: Warpaint
Street Armor.description: Warpaint is the common term for the bizarre combat fashions and scrap-built street harness of gangers, cult enforcers, street toughs, and other marginal sorts with little money but much need for protection. An NPC in warpaint that is meaningful to them gains a +1 Morale bonus.

Street Armor.name: Armored Undersuit
Street Armor.description: An armored undersuit is a skin-tight bodysuit woven of advanced TL4 fibers with exceptional shock-activated rigidity and impact dispersion capabilities. Transparent panels allow it to be worn with almost any outfit without drawing notice.

Street Armor.name: Secure Clothing
Street Armor.description: Secure clothing comes in assorted styles and fashions ranging from casual street wear to haute couture. Normal fabrics and components are replaced with light, flexible armor components that are only slightly hindering to the wearer.

Street Armor.name: Armored Vacc Suit
Street Armor.description: An armored vacc suit has traded off some comfort and flexibility for additional protective thickness. Aside from functioning as a normal vacc suit, it has only half the usual chance to tear when hit by an edged weapon or suit ripper.

Street Armor.name: Deflector Array
Street Armor.description: A deflector array consists of several force field nodes worn beneath ordinary clothing. The invisible shield it produces flares only when dangerous energies or impact is impending, glowing a brief, bright blue as it deflects the attack.

Combat Armor.name: Force Pavis
Combat Armor.description: A force pavis is a small pretech force disc projector that can absorb all manner of small arms fire. If the bearer's AC is already equal or better, the shield simply grants a +1 bonus to their AC. Shields render the bearer immune to the first instance of melee Shock they might otherwise suffer in a round.

Combat Armor.name: Security Armor
Combat Armor.description: Security armor is the ordinary working uniform of most law enforcement officials and security personnel. Various rigid plates and anti-ballistic panels provide protection for the wearer at minimal extra weight.

Combat Armor.name: Woven Body Armor
Combat Armor.description: Woven body armor represents the best armor that a TL3 world can manufacture, or an up-armored version of security armor used by TL4 high-threat response teams. The design is significantly more cumbersome, but allows for multiple layers of protection.

Combat Armor.name: Combat Field Uniform
Combat Armor.description: A combat field uniform is sophisticated battle dress fabricated from TL4 ablative coatings, rigid plates, and shock-activated soft components. The CFU is the standard uniform for well-equipped TL4 front-line soldiers.

Combat Armor.name: Icarus Harness
Combat Armor.description: The Icarus harness is a CFU upgrade for paratroopers, and replaces a conventional parachute with a crude gravity damper that allows the wearer to fall an unlimited distance without harm. Each fall over 3 meters drains a type A power cell. The suit also functions as a vacc suit for up to 30 minutes per vacc refresh.

Powered Armor.name: Vestimentum
Powered Armor.description: A "vestimentum" is a catch-all term for one of the many ancient Mandate ceremonial armors meant chiefly for parade guards, ritual officiants, cultural reenactors, or other roles that put elaborate style at a premium. While these outfits often look wildly unmilitary, their hyper-advanced components and micronized force fields give them the same protection against primitive weapons as any other powered armor.

Powered Armor.name: Assault Suit
Powered Armor.description: An assault suit represents the most sophisticated armor in common use among TL4 worlds. It requires a type B power cell for 24 hours of operation, and provides integral encrypted military comms, low-light and infrared vision, and a built-in energy feed interface. It also functions as a vacc suit so long as it remains powered, one that cannot be torn by edged weapons.

Powered Armor.name: Storm Armor
Powered Armor.description: Storm armor is a more advanced form of assault suit, one that can be fabricated only by those worlds that have retained some degree of Mandate-grade technical infrastructure. Its exo-augments allow the wearer to treat their Strength as 4 points higher for encumbrance purposes, and integral gravitic boosters allow the wearer to leap up to 20 meters or fall up to 40 meters without harm. Storm armor requires the same type B power cell as an assault suit.

Powered Armor.name: Field Emitter Panoply
Powered Armor.description: A field emitter panoply is a heavy-duty pretech defensive system composed of a half-dozen worn emitter nodes that sheath the wearer in a nimbus of close-fitting damper fields. It provides all the benefits of storm armor with no power source required, and is particularly effective at filtering radiation.

Ammo and Power.name: Ammo, 20 Rounds
Ammo and Power.description: For ease of play, ammunition can be used interchangeably with any projectile weapon. A cartridge of twenty rounds sufficient to reload most firearms.

Ammo and Power.name: Arrows
Ammo and Power.description: A bundle of twenty arrows, sized for use with a primitive bow, advanced bow, or conversion bow. Bows are uncommon weapons in the far future, though some lostworlder barbarians have nothing better.

Ammo and Power.name: Ammo, Missile
Ammo and Power.description: Some characters might have reason to pack along a man-portable rocket launcher, or have one mounted on their favorite gravcar. Heavy weapons and their ammunition are usually outlawed for civilians on most worlds.

Ammo and Power.name: Power Cell, Type A
Ammo and Power.description: Power cells are small cylindrical objects designed to take and hold electrical charges. Type A cells are usually used for personal equipment. Power cells can be recharged off a ship's power plant or other grid; recharging requires 30 minutes for a type A cell.

Ammo and Power.name: Power Cell, Type B
Ammo and Power.description: Power cells are small cylindrical objects designed to take and hold electrical charges. The larger type B cells are used for vehicles and heavy gear. Recharging a type B cell requires 24 hours.

Ammo and Power.name: Solar Recharger
Ammo and Power.description: This recharger unfolds into a 2 meter by 2 meter square field of solar cells. Granted a primary star of roughly Earth-like intensity, it can recharge one type A power cell per day.

Ammo and Power.name: Telekinetic Generator
Ammo and Power.description: While this device assumes the presence of a trained telekinetic, it isn't strictly psitech, as its operation is quite simple. A telekinetic user pushes a resistance bar within the generator, causing a flow of electricity to recharge an attached power cell.

Communications.name: Comm Server
Communications.description: A powerful base unit for providing communications without comsats. The server provides service between up to three dozen compads within 300 kilometers of the unit, with all transmissions heavily encrypted.

Communications.name: Compad
Communications.description: One of a host of different hand-held portable communications devices. Most TL4 worlds have global comm coverage, but primitive worlds render these devices useless without a nearby comm server to provide connectivity.

Communications.name: Field Radio
Communications.description: On worlds too primitive to have a comm grid, adventurers often fall back on these headset-mounted field radios. A single type A cell powers them for months of use.

Communications.name: Translator Torc
Communications.description: Each translator torc is keyed for two languages, and will automatically translate what it hears in one into speech in the other. Any attempts to exert social skills or Charisma through a translator torc suffer a -2 skill check penalty.

Computing Gear.name: Black Slab
Computing Gear.description: While a "black slab" appears to be a normal dataslab to casual examination, these devices are packed with intrusion-optimization hardware and integral line tapping tools, granting a +1 bonus to all hacking attempts made with them. They are quite illegal on most worlds.

Computing Gear.name: Data Phase Tap
Computing Gear.description: This handheld device can detect data lines within five meters through up to ten centimeters of ordinary walls, and can generate an energy manipulation field allowing tapping of that data line for hacking purposes without physically damaging the wall.

Computing Gear.name: Data Protocol
Computing Gear.description: Not so much a device as a collection of standard manuals on a world's particular data formats and security methodologies. The price listed is for black-market manuals on worlds where this information is rigidly restricted.

Computing Gear.name: Dataslab
Computing Gear.description: A palm-sized computing device that can unfold into a thin slab roughly one-third of a meter on a side. It can perform all the functions of a compad or handheld computer and can communicate wirelessly with nearby devices.

Computing Gear.name: Line Shunt
Computing Gear.description: These palm-sized discs have an adhesive side that will stick to virtually anything and a polychromatic phased compound on its shell that shifts color to blend with its surroundings, allowing access to well-defended computerized systems.

Computing Gear.name: Remote Link Unit
Computing Gear.description: These data broadcast link units have been preloaded with one-time pad security measures, advanced stealth circuitry, and sophisticated data progression algorithms. Two of these links allow a user to maintain contact with a remote data storage unit.

Computing Gear.name: Stiletto Charge
Computing Gear.description: These ancient Mandate-era polymorphic intrusion charges were originally made to allow Mandate agents to easily overcome primitive colonial data security measures. When used as part of a hack against a TL4 system, it causes the skill check to automatically succeed. These devices are single-use, and are prized so highly that they are almost always unavailable for conventional purchase.

Computing Gear.name: Storage Unit
Computing Gear.description: While conventional dataslabs have ample space to hold any reasonable amount of data, sometimes a party needs to store or acquire a truly huge dataset. This standard TL4 storage unit is a portable but clumsy case hardened against anything short of intentional damage with a firearm.

Computing Gear.name: Tightbeam Link Unit
Computing Gear.description: Much like a remote link unit, a tightbeam unit uses a laser to connect via line-of-sight transmission. There's almost no chance for a conventional security system to detect this link, but it requires that the infiltrators get a clear line of sight between the unit and the receiving end.

Field Equipment.name: Atmofilter
Field Equipment.description: This face mask can filter out most atmospheric toxins. Attaching a standard vacc suit oxygen bottle to a belt-mounted feed will also supply a breathable atmosphere for up to six hours.

Field Equipment.name: Backpack (Primitive)
Field Equipment.description: A worn backpack counts as a readied item, though objects stowed inside it still require the usual round to dig free. A more advanced TL4 backpack is effectively without encumbrance, albeit costlier.

Field Equipment.name: Backpack (TL4)
Field Equipment.description: TL4 versions of the backpack are effectively without encumbrance, albeit they cost 50 credits. A worn backpack counts as a readied item, though objects stowed inside it still require the usual round to dig free.

Field Equipment.name: Binoculars
Field Equipment.description: Standard 7x50 binoculars.

Field Equipment.name: Binoculars, Low-Light
Field Equipment.description: TL4 binoculars with integral low-light optics and up to 25x150 power. They require a type A power cell for up to a week of regular usage.

Field Equipment.name: Climbing Harness
Field Equipment.description: A collection of straps, ropes, pitons, and other climbing aids that grant a +1 bonus on any Exert climbing skill test. Using a climbing harness is noisy, and any Sneak skill checks while climbing with one suffer a -2 penalty.

Field Equipment.name: Glowbug
Field Equipment.description: A palm-sized disc that can adhere to any non-porous surface. When turned on, it emits a white light, illuminating everything within ten meters for twenty-four hours. A hundred glowbugs can be recharged off a single type A cell.

Field Equipment.name: Grapnel Launcher
Field Equipment.description: This launcher fires a rope up to forty meters. The rope can bear up to a metric ton of weight, though extremely heavy weights or a precarious hit can cause the grapnel to pull free. A type A power cell fuels six shots from a launcher.

Field Equipment.name: Grav Chute
Field Equipment.description: When this cylinder is strapped to a person or object and activated, it smoothly modulates falling speeds for up to 1000 meters. The chute can safely slow up to 300 kilos of weight, and burns out after one use.

Field Equipment.name: Grav Chute, Orbital
Field Equipment.description: A TL5 grav chute capable of operating from orbital heights. Like the standard version, it burns out after one use.

Field Equipment.name: Grav Harness
Field Equipment.description: This advanced gravitic harness allows clumsy flight at a rate of 20 meters per round as a Main Action. It requires a type B power cell to fuel it, and the miniaturized electronics consume the cell in five minutes of operation. It can lift up to 200 kilos.

Field Equipment.name: Instapanel
Field Equipment.description: In its compressed form, an instapanel is a two-kilo cube of ceraplast five centimeters on a side. When a type A power cell is inserted, it immediately expands to an opaque, waterproof ceraplast sheet 2 meters on each side that hardens into a tough, rigid shape after five minutes.

Field Equipment.name: Low-Light Goggles
Field Equipment.description: These goggles provide a monochrome but serviceable view out to the wearer's normal visual distance, provided that there is any illumination available at all. A type A power cell will operate these goggles for a week.

Field Equipment.name: Navcomp
Field Equipment.description: A combination of low-tech compasses, automappers, astronomic charts, and gyroscopes packed into a flat, one-kilo case. A character with a navcomp will never get lost on worlds with GPS satellites.

Field Equipment.name: Portabox
Field Equipment.description: A small cube of ceraplast attached to an electronic keycard. When a type A power cell is inserted, the portabox immediately unfolds into a rigid locker with 1.5 x 1 x 1 meter dimensions, air-tight and electronically locked.

Field Equipment.name: Pressure Tent
Field Equipment.description: This tent maintains a breathable atmosphere, tolerable temperature and serviceable sleeping quarters for up to five very friendly occupants. A single standard vacc suit oxygen tank can provide breathable air for the occupants for up to 24 hours.

Field Equipment.name: Rations, 1 Day
Field Equipment.description: Dried or otherwise preserved foodstuffs sufficient for one day. If water is not otherwise available, add another item's worth of encumbrance for the water necessary for a person's daily needs.

Field Equipment.name: Rope, 20 Meters
Field Equipment.description: Light and sturdy rope. A synthetic TL4 version counts as one encumbrance item per 40 meters and costs 40 credits.

Field Equipment.name: Rope, Synthetic (40 Meters)
Field Equipment.description: A metatool can be used to cut and join the synthetics used in TL4 rope, which counts as one encumbrance item per 40 meters.

Field Equipment.name: Scout Report
Field Equipment.description: A collation of survey scans and merchant reports on a particular lost world or isolated colony. Scouting reports provide maps, basic information, and note any critical cultural taboos.

Field Equipment.name: Survey Scanner
Field Equipment.description: A multipurpose scanner that can take atmospheric and gravitic readings, provide basic chemical analysis of samples of up to one cubic centimeter in size, and record up to two hundred hours of video information.

Field Equipment.name: Survival Kit
Field Equipment.description: A standard belt-worn kit with fire lighter, water filter, three thermal flares, knife, thermal blanket, waterproof tarp, a glowbug, and a radio beacon. Possession of a survival kit grants a +1 to all relevant Survive skill checks.

Field Equipment.name: Telescoping Pole
Field Equipment.description: Retracting to a 30-centimeter baton, this pole extends and locks into a 3.048-meter extension that can bear as much as a thousand kilograms of weight or serve as a makeshift club.

Field Equipment.name: Thermal Flare
Field Equipment.description: If triggered in one mode, the flare burns with a bright white light for two hours. If the guidance fins are extended first, the flare launches up to 200 meters and explodes in a bright white flash, doing 1d6 damage to anyone it hits.

Field Equipment.name: Trade Goods
Field Equipment.description: Glowbugs, ceramic fire lighters, antibiotics, ceraplast tools, and the other fruits of a TL4 civilization that might be valuable on more primitive worlds. A kilo of trade goods can usually be traded for at least a hundred credits worth of local products.

Field Equipment.name: Trade Metals
Field Equipment.description: The fruit of common TL4 asteroid mining, trade metals include gold, platinum, artificial gemstones, and other substances precious on many lost worlds and trivially valuable on space-faring ones.

Field Equipment.name: Vacc Fresher
Field Equipment.description: This three-kilo tube filters and compresses atmosphere to refill vacc suit oxygen tanks. It can extract oxygen from any atmosphere which contains it, even in the form of carbon dioxide.

Field Equipment.name: Vacc Skin
Field Equipment.description: A more advanced TL5 version of the vacc suit, this skin-tight suit can be worn as a readied item in conjunction with armor, though it grants no Armor Class bonus itself. It requires no oxygen tank, automatically cracking and recycling the wearer's respiration.

Field Equipment.name: Vacc Suit
Field Equipment.description: The standard TL4 vacc suit is designed to allow the wearer to survive in both hard vacuum and on most inhospitable planetary surfaces. Vacc suits are cumbersome, and apply a -2 penalty to all hit rolls and skill checks that require movement. No armor can be worn with a vacc suit, though the suit itself grants AC 13 to its wearers.

Pharmaceuticals.name: Bezoar
Pharmaceuticals.description: Heal-1. A complex antibiotic cocktail, Bezoar is an effective default treatment for a wide variety of infectious diseases. Each application adds 1 System Strain to the target, and it cannot cure cancers, bioweapons, or congenital diseases.

Pharmaceuticals.name: Brainwave
Pharmaceuticals.description: Heal-2. This psitech drug requires advanced TL5 facilities to compound. Application gives a psychic 2 extra maximum Effort for one hour, after which they suffer 4 points of System Strain.

Pharmaceuticals.name: Hush
Pharmaceuticals.description: Heal-0. An extremely heavy neurotranquilizer, Hush leaves the subject awake and responsive to simple, untaxing commands. A subject must be immobilized or willing to be affected by it.

Pharmaceuticals.name: Lift
Pharmaceuticals.description: Heal-0. A Lift stim augments and amplifies the body's natural response to physical injury and exhaustion, healing 1d8 plus the user's Heal skill in hit points after five minutes of rest. Each application adds 1 System Strain to the target.

Pharmaceuticals.name: Psych
Pharmaceuticals.description: A military drug duplicated in rougher form by many street chemists, Psych fills the user with an intense sense of confidence and reckless courage, granting a Morale score of 12 and a +1 bonus on all skill checks for fifteen minutes, but adds 1 System Strain and is highly psychologically addictive.

Pharmaceuticals.name: Pretech Cosmetic
Pharmaceuticals.description: Before the Silence stims existed for a host of cosmetic, hygiene, and health purposes. The basic pretech stim substrate also works to heal 1d6 lost hit points in the user at a cost of 1 System Strain.

Pharmaceuticals.name: Reverie
Pharmaceuticals.description: Heal-1. This very dangerous combat drug completely subdues the subject's fear centers and adrenaline production, leaving them perfectly calm even in the midst of mortal danger, though slowed to acting only on even-numbered combat rounds and taking double damage. Lasts ten minutes and adds 2 System Strain.

Pharmaceuticals.name: Squeal
Pharmaceuticals.description: Heal-1. This "truth serum" is unreliable but still one of the best available options for field interrogations. The subject must be immobilized or willing to be affected by it.

Pharmaceuticals.name: Tsunami
Pharmaceuticals.description: Heal-1. An emergency combat stim used to juice certain expendable soldiers before an assault. Subjects gain a Morale score of 12, 10 extra hit points for ten minutes and a +2 bonus on all hit rolls. Each application adds 2 System Strain to the target.

Tools and Medical.name: Bioscanner
Tools and Medical.description: While an untrained user can use this tool to discern internal bleeding, gross physical distress, or toxins in a plant or animal, it requires Heal-0 skill to use it to its fullest. One type A power cell will power it for up to twenty-four hours of regular usage.

Tools and Medical.name: Lazarus Patch
Tools and Medical.description: A vital tool for adventurers, the lazarus patch is a heavy compress laced with antibiotics, coagulants, system stabilizers, plasma, and a one-shot diagnostic suite. If applied to a character at 0 hit points, allows an Int/Heal or Dex/Heal check to stabilize the subject.

Tools and Medical.name: Medkit
Tools and Medical.description: Containing a broad supply of pharmaceuticals, spray bandages, glue sutures, and a succinct handbook of injury care, the medkit is designed for handling sudden and drastic injuries as well as long-term recuperative care.

Tools and Medical.name: Metatool
Tools and Medical.description: This wrist-mounted housing contains a myriad of small, useful tools designed to handle the widest possible range of technical needs. While a metatool is too limited to handle major jobs, it is usually sufficient to manage jury-rigged repairs and temporary fixes.

Tools and Medical.name: Spare Parts
Tools and Medical.description: A general category for a number of small TL4 components and repair materials. While a simple toolkit or metatool is often enough to fix a damaged object, severely broken devices may need replacement parts.

Tools and Medical.name: Tailored Antiallergens
Tools and Medical.description: A dose of tailored antiallergens can be used to render a local world's organics largely edible by humans and its atmosphere breathable without severe allergic reactions. A dose lasts for twenty-four hours.

Tools and Medical.name: Toolkit, Postech
Tools and Medical.description: Containing a wide range of necessary tools for a particular skill set, toolkits can handle almost any job that doesn't require a full-scale shop or lab. A standard postech toolkit can handle electronics, small welding jobs, and basic repair on ordinary TL4 goods.

Tools and Medical.name: Toolkit, Pretech
Tools and Medical.description: More sophisticated pretech tools are necessary for working on advanced TL5 artifacts, and the tools themselves are very rare and difficult to obtain.
